mechanism: Oxybutynin's anticholinergic properties may impair gastric motility and delay glipizide absorption, while oxybutynin is metabolized by CYP3A4 which may have minor interactions with glipizide metabolism; both drugs can cause hyperglycemia through different mechanisms.
action: Monitor blood glucose levels more frequently; counsel patient on hypoglycemia symptoms; consider alternative anticholinergic agent if hyperglycemia develops.
